children: Asian stock markets traded lower on Thursday, following overnight declines on Wall Street after a rise in U.S. Treasury yields and sustained geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. With Brent crude holding near elevated levels, concerns over inflation, import costs, and central bank policy continued to weigh on regional sentiment ahead of upcoming U.S. inflation data and the Federal Reserve’s September meeting.
U.S. equity futures held steady, Nasdaq futures flat +0.02%, S&P 500 futures up 0.20%, and Dow futures up 0.34%.
In commodities, crude oil rose to about $96.70 a barrel, while spot gold held steady near $4,400 an ounce.
South Korea’s KOSPI down 0.15% to around 6,920, reversing previous gains even as South Korea and France agreed to deepen bilateral cooperation in AI and semiconductors.
